calls.head: Nobody’s sitting back in this one
calls.body: Buffalo plays some of the league’s fastest games, and so does Columbus. We think this one runs hotter than either team’s usual.
calls.call: The game runs at more than 84.5 shots per 60 at 5-on-5, faster than either team’s usual.
calls.nums: Pace (shots per 60 at 5-on-5, both teams): Buffalo 6th (84.1), Columbus 4th (84.5)
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 0 and 0 games this season
calls.happened: The game ran at 62.4 shots per 60 at 5-on-5, both teams combined, against the faster team’s usual 84.5 and a league average of 81.7.

calls.head: The Sabres kill penalties far better than the Blue Jackets
calls.body: On the penalty kill, Buffalo is around the middle of the league and Columbus is the league’s worst. That’s about as far apart as two teams get.
calls.call: The Sabres’ penalty kill allows less per 60 than the Blue Jackets’.
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 0 and 0 games this season
calls.happened: On expected goals allowed per 60 on the penalty kill, Buffalo had 10.7 per 60 and Columbus 7.5 per 60. Coming in, Buffalo was at 7.5 per 60 and Columbus at 8.5 per 60.

CBJ.head: We had this close to even (55% for Columbus), and Columbus came through.

BUF.head: We had this close to even (45% for Buffalo), and it went Columbus’s way.

surprises.head: A rough night for U. Luukkonen
surprises.body: U. Luukkonen allowed 5 goals on shots worth 2.2 expected goals, 2.8 more than expected. Starting goalies had a night this rough about once every 25 starts over the last three seasons.

surprises.head: Columbus brought the hits
surprises.body: Columbus’s hit score in the close stretches of the game was 163, against their usual 99 (100 is league average, adjusted for the arena’s scorer). A team strays this far about once every 25 games.

story.head: The Blue Jackets beat the Sabres
paras: Mattias Samuelsson opened the scoring midway through the first. Matthew Knies added two goals. Five different Blue Jackets scored.

The score flatters the Blue Jackets: the Sabres had the better of the play. Replay the chances a hundred times and the Sabres win about six in ten. By our Swing measure, Owen Power had the best night of anyone, even in a loss.
